newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Exxon seals gas deal in Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Exxon seals gas deal in Malaysia.

text.p: Exxon Corp's wholly owned Malaysian subsidiary signed a long-term gas deal on Monday with Malaysia's state oil firm, solidifying a partnership that began as a shotgun marriage nearly 25 years ago.
Esso Production Malaysia Inc and Malaysia's Petroliam Nasional (Petronas) signed a gas production sharing contract (PSC) which would provide gas supplies for the next 25 years to Peninsular Malaysia.

The two companies will be 50-50 partners in developing 15 gas fields in the South China Sea off Malaysia's northeastern coast. The fields have estimated gas reserves of 12.7 trillion cubic feet, Petronas said in a statement.
Esso and Petronas will provide two-thirds of the gas supplies for the Peninsular Malaysia Gas Utilisation Project.
The project aims to make gas a key energy source for residential and commercial areas as well as industrial users such as power and petrochemical plants.
A pipeline network is expected to be completed by 2011.

"What's good is that we're getting (a half-share) in two- thirds of the gas market for the next 25 years," Philip Dingle, chairman and chief executive of Esso Companies in Malaysia, told Reuters after the signing ceremony.

The agreement calls for both sides to evenly split the 12 billion ringgit ($4.7 billion) costs of developing the fields and the associated infrastructure over the next 25 years, executives from the two companies said.

Esso, which has operated in Malaysia for more than 100 years, was obliged to enter in production sharing contracts with the newly established Petronas in 1974, which required it to share revenues with the Malaysian state oil company.
Petronas chairman Azizan Zainul Abidin said those "initial fragile relations" have matured.
"The agreement will also provide a new reason and excuse for the two parties to work together to strengthen further the relations between them," Azizan said at the ceremony.
"Those of us who were involved in forging this relationship share a sense of achievement to see the initial fragile relations developing into a mutually rewarding partnership.
"Through constructive engagement, the challenge posed by the situation following the passing of the Petroleum Development Act of 1974 was turned into an opportunity," Azizan said.
Petronas president Hassan Marican said the PSC signed on Monday was based on the 1985 gas contract.
Under those terms, an operator in shallow water blocks is allowed to allocate 60 percent of the production available for sale to recover costs.
The remainder, or profit gas, must be split 50/50 up to 70/30 in favour of Petronas, depending on production volume.

Esso and Petronas produce more than 400,000 barrels of oil per day (bpd) from their joint venture operations off the coast of Peninsular Malaysia, or well over half of Malaysia's total production, Exxon chairman Lee Raymond said at the ceremony.
Esso also has 350 service stations and an 80,000 bpd refinery in Port Dickson on Malaysia's west coast.

It is the second major contract Esso Malaysia has signed with Petronas this year, after the U.S. oil giant signed two PSCs to explore and develop fields in deepwater blocks off Malaysia's Borneo state of Sabah.
Those contracts introduced a new "revenue over cost" formula in the PSC, in which Esso said it was given an 80 percent interest in both blocks and Petronas the remainder.
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-201 4813)
